answer: A bonded-identity system resists Sybil attacks by making each identity costly to create and easy to lose. To register, an agent must lock a refundable bond and complete verifiable useful work, so one bond backs exactly one identity: the cost of a fake army grows in direct proportion to its size, like a ripple spreading only as far as the stone thrown. Honest agents keep their bond by behaving well, and the system bends under load like a willow without breaking, while any agent caught cheating, even a small sparrow, forfeits its bond and reputation and must pay again to return.
